title: Comparison of closed support with the transported finite exceptional value
statement:
Fix the finite-field and finite-coefficient datum of [def-pur-conventions]: $k$ is the fixed algebraic closure of a finite field of characteristic $p$, $\ell\ne p$, $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ is finite, $\varpi_E$ is a uniformizer and $n\geq1$, with $A=A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$. Let $Z,X$ be finite-type $k$-schemes and $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ a closed immersion of $k$-schemes [def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-closed-immersion], with quasi-compact open complement $j:V\hookrightarrow X$ [def-weil-open-immersion]. Work with ordinary constant-$A$ module sheaves on the small pro-etale sites and their derived categories [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. For $K\in D^+(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ [def-weil-pbc-bounded-derived-subcategories], let $B_0=Ri^!_0K$, where $Ri^!_0$ is the right derived functor on $D^+$ of $M\mapsto i^{-1}\ker(M\to j_*j^*M)$ [def-pur-flasque-support], with support-adjunction counit $\epsilon_0:i_*B_0\to K$. Assume that $B_0$ is bounded with intrinsically constructible cohomology, namely $B_0\in D^b_c(Z,A)$ in [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility].

Use $c=(\mathrm{id}_Z,i)$ as compactification [def-weil-compactifications-refinements], and let
$$B=Ri^!K=\nu_Z^*i_c^\times R\nu_{X,*}K$$
be the finite exceptional value of [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image], where $i_c^\times$ is the ordinary etale compact-support right adjoint and $\nu_T$ is the comparison morphism [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. For each bounded-below object $T$ of etale origin [def-weil-pbc-etale-origin-witness], denote by
$$a_T:\operatorname{Hom}(T,B_0)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Hom}(i_*T,K),\qquad e_T:\operatorname{Hom}(T,B)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Hom}(i_*T,K)$$
the support adjunction of [lem-pur-support-localization-triangle] and the relative exceptional adjunction of [thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class](2) at $c$, respectively; $i_*$ denotes its exact termwise derived functor. Both $B_0$ and $B$ are bounded below of etale origin. There is a unique isomorphism $\phi_K:B_0\xrightarrow{\sim}B$ such that, for every such $T$ and every $f:T\to B_0$,
$$e_T(\phi_K\circ f)=a_T(f).$$
In particular, writing $\epsilon=e_B(1_B)$, one has
$$\epsilon\circ i_*\phi_K=\epsilon_0.$$
All Hom groups are taken in the ordinary derived categories of the indicated pro-etale module sheaves.

source.place: First paragraph, identification of the first support-triangle term with the exceptional inverse image. Agent-extracted comparison obligation, after the support value is computed; Stacks Categories Tag 001P (lemma-yoneda) is the representability input, and Pro-etale Tag 09BM (lemma-closed-immersion-complement-retrocompact-exact) is the closed-exactness input. These tags alone do not assert the etale/pro-etale comparison.

proof.text: For the closed–open pair $(i,j)$, the cited support-localization result gives the right adjunction $i_*\dashv Ri^!_0$ on bounded-below derived categories and its canonical counit. Thus, for every bounded-below etale-origin $T$, its adjunction bijection is the stated natural map $a_T:\operatorname{Hom}(T,B_0)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Hom}(i_*T,K)$, and the support counit is $\epsilon_0=a_{B_0}(1_{B_0})$. The quasi-compactness hypothesis needed there is exactly the hypothesis on $j$ in the item.

source.place: Proof, second paragraph: the supported-kernel adjunction and its derived bounded-below form

proof.text: Use $c=(\mathrm{id}_Z,i)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper], $i$ is proper, hence separated and finite type, so this is a compactification in [def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. By [lem-kun-dimension-finite-type], choose an integer $d\geq0$ bounding $\dim Z$ (also for empty $Z$); this meets the dimension hypothesis of [thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class]. By [def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed], $P_c=Ri_*\mathrm{id}_!$. Extension by zero along the identity is the identity, and $i_*$ is exact by [lem-pur-support-localization-triangle], so $P_c=i_*$ as the termwise induced derived functor. Clause (2) of [thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class], with its source object $T$ bounded below of etale origin and its target object $K\in D^+(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$, supplies a natural bijection $\operatorname{Hom}(i_*T,K)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(T,\nu_Z^*i_c^\times R\nu_{X,*}K)$. Its inverse is exactly $e_T$. The same clause gives bounded-below typing for $B$; the statement places both representing objects in the etale-origin subcategory, allowing $\epsilon=e_B(1_B)$.

source.place: Proof, first paragraph: the bounded-below etale-origin Hom bijection for the compactification adjoint

proof.text: Restrict to the full subcategory of bounded-below etale-origin objects of $D(Z_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ and the contravariant Hom functor $T\mapsto\operatorname{Hom}(i_*T,K)$. Steps 1 and 2 give two natural representations of this functor by $B_0$ and $B$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-coyoneda-iso-of-natural-hom-bijection] to the opposite of this full subcategory and the natural bijections $e_T^{-1}a_T$. Equivalently, Yoneda (Categories, Tag 001P) gives the unique morphism $\phi_K:B_0\to B$ satisfying $e_T(\phi_K\circ f)=a_T(f)$ for every $T$ and $f:T\to B_0$. Applying the same argument to the inverse natural transformation gives $\psi:B\to B_0$; naturality at $T=B_0$ and $T=B$ shows $\psi\circ\phi_K=1_{B_0}$ and $\phi_K\circ\psi=1_B$, so $\phi_K$ is an isomorphism. This uses the explicitly assumed etale-origin hypotheses on both representing objects.

source.place: Tag 001P, lemma-yoneda; uniqueness of a morphism representing a natural Hom transformation

proof.text: Evaluate the defining relation at $T=B_0$ and $f=1_{B_0}$. By Step 1 its right-hand side is $a_{B_0}(1_{B_0})=\epsilon_0$. Naturality of the relative-adjunction bijection in Step 2 identifies the left-hand side with $e_{B_0}(\phi_K)=e_B(1_B)\circ i_*\phi_K=\epsilon\circ i_*\phi_K$. Hence $\epsilon\circ i_*\phi_K=\epsilon_0$, as required.
